title.zh: 卷400 列傳一百八十七 何桂珍 徐豐玉 张汝瀛 金雲门 唐树义 岳兴阿 易容之 温绍原 金光箸 李孟群 赵景贤
title.en: Volume 400 Biographies 187: He Guizhen, Xu Fengyu, Zhang Ruying, Jin Yunmen, Tang Shuyi, Yue Xing A, Yi Rongzhi, Wen Shaoyuan, Jin Guangzhu, Li Mengqun, Zhao Jingxian
title.raw: 卷400 列傳一百八十七 何桂珍 徐豐玉 张汝瀛 金雲门 唐树义 岳兴阿 易容之 温绍原 金光箸 李孟群 赵景贤

sentences.zh: =何桂珍=何桂珍，字丹畦，雲南師宗人。

translations.literal: = He Guizhen = He Guizhen, styled Danqi, was a native of Shizong in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He Guizhen, styled Danqi, was from Shizong in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，年甫冠，乞假歸娶。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and while still barely of age requested leave to return home and marry.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the eighteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and, still scarcely twenty, took leave to go home and marry.

sentences.zh: 散館授編修，督貴州學政。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the academy he was appointed compiler and supervised education in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his academy term he was made a compiler and served as educational commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 入直上書房，授孚郡王讀。

translations.literal: He entered the Southern Study and instructed the Prince of Fu in reading.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the imperial study and tutored the Prince of Fu.

sentences.zh: 文宗在潛邸，即受知。

translations.literal: While the future Wenzong was still in his princely residence, He already won his favor.
translations.idiomatic: He had already won the future Emperor Wenzong's trust while the emperor was still heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 桂珍鄉試出倭仁門，與唐鑑、曾國籓為師友，學以宋儒為宗。

translations.literal: Guizhen had passed the provincial examination under Woren; with Tang Jian and Zeng Guofan he was teacher and friend alike, taking Song Neo-Confucian learning as his standard.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhen had been a provincial examination pupil of Woren; he counted Tang Jian and Zeng Guofan among his teachers and friends, and took Song Neo-Confucianism as his guiding tradition.

sentences.zh: 及文宗即位，以所撰大學衍義芻言奏進，優詔嘉納。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended the throne, Guizhen presented his draft Expository Remarks on the Great Learning and received an edict of special praise and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenzong took the throne, Guizhen submitted his Expository Remarks on the Great Learning and received a warmly approving imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 數上疏論時政得失，言琦善、牛鑑僨軍之將，不宜任兵事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on the gains and losses of current policy, saying that Qishan and Niu Jian were generals who had ruined their armies and were unfit to be entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly on current affairs, arguing that Qishan and Niu Jian were commanders who had ruined their armies and should not be put in charge of military operations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，出為福建興泉永道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he went out to serve as intendant of Xing, Quan, and Yong in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was posted as intendant of the Xing-Quan-Yong circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 巡防大臣賈楨等奏請開缺，留京隨辦城守事宜。

translations.literal: The capital defense commissioners Jia Zhen and others memorialized to have his post declared vacant and to keep him in the capital to assist with city defense.
translations.idiomatic: Capital defense commissioners including Jia Zhen asked that his post be left vacant so he could remain in Beijing to help with the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 四年，畿輔解嚴，授安徽徽寧池太廣道。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the metropolitan region was relieved from martial law, he was appointed intendant of the Huining, Chitai, and Guang circuits in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after martial law in the capital region was lifted, he was appointed intendant of the Huining-Chitai-Guang circuit in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 安慶久陷，巡撫福濟駐廬州之店埠。

translations.literal: Anqing had long been lost, and the governor Fuiji was stationed at Dianbu in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing had been in rebel hands for a long time, and Governor Fuiji was encamped at Dianbu in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 桂珍所治在江南，阻於賊，遂留江北。

translations.literal: The territory Guizhen was to administer lay south of the Yangzi, but he was blocked by the rebels and therefore remained north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhen's jurisdiction lay south of the Yangzi, but rebel lines kept him on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 檄募勇從征，餉無所出，久之，得二百人，至霍山，號召鄉團，增為三千人，激以忠義，破捻匪李兆受於霍城，追擊至麻埠，進逼流波甿；

translations.literal: He issued orders to recruit braves for the campaign, but had no funds for pay; after a long time he obtained two hundred men, reached Huoshan, summoned local militia, and increased his force to three thousand; rousing them with loyalty and righteousness, he defeated the Nian bandit Li Zhaoshou at Huocheng, pursued him to Mapu, and pressed on toward Liubomeng;
translations.idiomatic: He called up volunteers for the campaign but had no money for their pay; only after a long delay did he raise two hundred men. At Huoshan he rallied local militia until his force reached three thousand. Stirring them with appeals to loyalty, he routed the Nian leader Li Zhaoshou at Huocheng, chased him to Mapu, and advanced on Liubomeng;

sentences.zh: 檄商城、固始鄉團截其北，金寨練勇拒其東，自率所部遏其西，兆受大懼，與其黨馬超江等同降，解散脅從萬計，民歡呼載道，饋糗糧不絕。

translations.literal: He ordered the militia of Shangcheng and Gushi to cut off the north, the trained braves of Jinzhai to block the east, and led his own troops to hold the west; Zhaoshou was greatly afraid, and he and his follower Ma Chaojiang and others surrendered together, disbanding tens of thousands who had been coerced; the people cheered along the roads and brought provisions without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered militia from Shangcheng and Gushi to block the north, trained volunteers from Jinzhai to hold the east, and led his own men to seal the west. Terrified, Zhaoshou surrendered with his lieutenant Ma Chaojiang and others, releasing tens of thousands of coerced followers. The people cheered in the streets and kept bringing food without end.

sentences.zh: 福濟令桂珍援廬江，檄至，城已陷，馳救不及，劾罷職。

translations.literal: Fuiji ordered Guizhen to relieve Lujiang, but when the order arrived the city had already fallen and he could not reach it in time; he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Fuiji ordered Guizhen to relieve Lujiang, but by the time the order arrived the city had fallen and he could not save it; he was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 是年，曾國籓破賊田家鎮，進圍九江，桂珍通牒言戰狀，國籓以聞。

translations.literal: That year Zeng Guofan defeated the rebels at Tianjiazhen and advanced to besiege Jiujiang; Guizhen sent dispatches reporting the state of battle, and Zeng reported them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zeng Guofan routed the rebels at Tianjiazhen and moved to besiege Jiujiang. Guizhen sent battle reports, which Zeng forwarded to court.

sentences.zh: 袁甲三軍臨淮，欲資桂珍兵西與楚師會，至蘄水而九江軍失利，武昌再陷。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiasan's army was at Linhuai and wished to use Guizhen's troops to move west and join the Hunan forces, but when they reached Qishui the Jiujiang army suffered defeat and Wuchang fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiasan's army was at Linhuai and hoped to use Guizhen's troops to march west and join the Hunan army, but at Qishui the force at Jiujiang was beaten and Wuchang fell again.

sentences.zh: 國籓入江西，文報不相聞。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan entered Jiangxi, and dispatches no longer reached one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan marched into Jiangxi, and communications between them broke off.

sentences.zh: 桂珍乃提孤軍轉戰潛、霍間。

translations.literal: Guizhen then led his isolated army to fight back and forth between Qian and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhen then led a lone force fighting between Qian and Huo.

sentences.zh: 五年春，克蘄水、英山，殲賊首田金爵。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he captured Qishui and Yingshan and destroyed the rebel leader Tian Jinjue.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he took Qishui and Yingshan and killed the rebel chief Tian Jinjue.

sentences.zh: 和春上其功，予六品頂戴，留駐英山。

translations.literal: He Chun reported his merit, and he was granted a sixth-rank official's cap button and remained stationed at Yingshan.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun commended his achievements; he was given a sixth-rank cap button and stayed on at Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 自桂珍受事，至是八閱月，僅支餉銀三百兩。

translations.literal: From the time Guizhen took office until then, eight months had passed, and he had received only three hundred taels of silver in pay.
translations.idiomatic: In the eight months since Guizhen had taken command, he had received only three hundred taels of pay.

sentences.zh: 民團相從者踵至，益以李兆受降眾，餓不得食，五月，師遂潰。

translations.literal: Local militia followers arrived in an unbroken stream, and with them were added the men who had surrendered under Li Zhaoshou; starving and unable to eat, in the fifth month the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Militia volunteers kept joining him, and Li Zhaoshou's surrendered men swelled the ranks, but they went hungry for lack of food; in the fifth month the force disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 兆受之降也，桂珍請福濟羈以官，不聽，不能無觖望。

translations.literal: When Zhaoshou had surrendered, Guizhen asked Fuiji to detain him with an official appointment, but Fuiji would not agree, and Zhaoshou could not help feeling resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaoshou surrendered, Guizhen asked Fuiji to keep him under control by giving him an official post, but Fuiji refused, and Zhaoshou could not help feeling slighted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，馬超江被殺，兆受乞拘仇，弗獲，則大恚，議為超江復仇，設位受吊，捻黨大集。

translations.literal: Before long Ma Chaojiang was killed; Zhaoshou asked that the killer be seized but failed to obtain him, and then was greatly enraged, proposing to avenge Chaojiang, setting up a mourning seat to receive condolences, and the Nian bands gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ma Chaojiang was killed. Zhaoshou demanded that the killer be arrested but was refused, and in a fury he vowed revenge for Chaojiang, set up a mourning altar, and Nian bands rallied in force.

sentences.zh: 於是安徽、河南皆以兆受复叛入告，兆受詣桂珍自陳，撫慰之，稍定。

translations.literal: Thereupon Anhui and Henan both reported that Zhaoshou had rebelled again; Zhaoshou came to Guizhen to explain himself, and Guizhen comforted him until matters were somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui and Henan then both reported that Zhaoshou had rebelled again. Zhaoshou came to Guizhen to plead his case; Guizhen reassured him and the situation calmed somewhat.

sentences.zh: 會福濟密書囑先發絕其患，書由驛遞，為兆受所得，謂桂珍賣己。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Fuiji sent a secret letter instructing that he be struck first to eliminate the threat; the letter went by courier post and was obtained by Zhaoshou, who believed Guizhen had betrayed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuiji then sent a secret letter ordering a preemptive strike to remove the threat. The message went by courier, fell into Zhaoshou's hands, and he concluded that Guizhen had sold him out.

sentences.zh: 十月，陽置酒，伏兵英山小南門外，桂珍遂遇害，左右四十餘人皆從死。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he pretended to host a banquet and set ambush troops outside the small south gate of Yingshan; Guizhen was thereupon killed, and more than forty of his attendants died with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he staged a feast and hid troops outside Yingshan's lesser south gate. Guizhen was murdered, and more than forty of his followers died with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，依道員陣亡例賜卹，贈光祿寺卿，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, condolence grants were given according to the precedent for an intendant killed in battle; he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and granted the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, he was mourned under the rules for an intendant killed in action, posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 同治初，江南平，曾國籓疏言桂珍率鄉團勦賊，飢餓艱難，歷人間未有之苦，機事不密，為叛人所戕，天下冤之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, when Jiangnan was pacified, Zeng Guofan memorialized that Guizhen had led local militia to suppress bandits amid hunger and hardship, suffering trials such as the world had never known, and that because plans were not kept secret he was slain by rebels—a wrong lamented throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, after Jiangnan was pacified, Zeng Guofan wrote that Guizhen had led militia against bandits through hunger and hardship beyond anything men had known, and that a leaked plan had let rebels kill him—a death the whole country regarded as unjust.

sentences.zh: 詔晉世職為騎都尉，予諡文貞，建祠英山縣。

translations.literal: An edict advanced his hereditary office to Commandant of Cavalry, granted the posthumous title Wenzhen, and ordered a shrine built in Yingshan County.
translations.idiomatic: An edict raised his hereditary rank to Commandant of Cavalry, gave him the posthumous title Wenzhen, and ordered a memorial shrine built in Yingshan County.

sentences.zh: =徐豐玉=徐豐玉，字石民，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: = Xu Fengyu = Xu Fengyu, styled Shimin, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fengyu, styled Shimin, was from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父鏞，嘉慶十四年進士，官至太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: His father Yong was a metropolitan graduate of the fourteenth year of Jiaqing and rose to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong became a metropolitan graduate in the fourteenth year of Jiaqing and rose to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 豐玉少應科舉不遇，捐納銓授貴州平遠知州。

translations.literal: Fengyu in his youth failed repeatedly at the examinations, purchased an office, and through the selection process was appointed magistrate of Pingyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu failed the civil examinations in his youth, bought an office, and was appointed magistrate of Pingyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 署威寧，捕斬大盜，總督林則徐嘉異之，調黃平。

translations.literal: Acting at Weining, he captured and executed a great bandit; Governor-General Lin Zexu praised his unusual merit and transferred him to Huangping.
translations.idiomatic: While acting magistrate at Weining he captured and executed a major outlaw. Governor-General Lin Zexu was impressed and moved him to Huangping.

sentences.zh: 苗寨盜魁保禾日聚眾剽掠。

translations.literal: In the Miao stockades the bandit chief Bao Heri gathered crowds to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Miao stockades the outlaw chief Bao Heri gathered men for raids.

sentences.zh: 豐玉清保甲，理屯軍，請兵會剿。

translations.literal: Fengyu cleared the baojia registers, organized garrison troops, and requested troops for a joint campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu reorganized the baojia militia system, put the garrison troops in order, and asked for regular troops for a joint suppression.

sentences.zh: 巡撫喬用遷慮激變，不許。

translations.literal: The governor Qiao Yongqian feared provoking an uprising and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Qiao Yongqian feared provoking a wider revolt and refused.

sentences.zh: 既而苗益恣，從知府胡林翼往剿，保禾遁。

translations.literal: Before long the Miao grew more unruly; he followed Prefect Hu Linyi on a punitive expedition, and Bao Heri fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao soon grew bolder. Fengyu joined Prefect Hu Linyi on a punitive expedition, and Bao Heri escaped.

sentences.zh: 時廣西匪起，蔓及貴州境。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Guangxi and spread into Guizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry had broken out in Guangxi and was spreading into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 豐玉練民兵，入山搜捕，多得盜魁，誅之。

translations.literal: Fengyu trained militia, entered the mountains to search and seize, captured many bandit chiefs, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu trained militia, hunted the mountains, captured many bandit leaders, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 雲南巡撫張亮基過黃平，悉其狀，密疏薦。

translations.literal: The Yunnan governor Zhang Liangji passed through Huangping, learned the full situation, and privately memorialized to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan Governor Zhang Liangji passed through Huangping he learned the full story and secretly recommended Fengyu to court.

sentences.zh: 遷郎岱同知，署思州府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to subprefect of Langdai and acted as prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to subprefect of Langdai and acted as prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，擢湖北黃州知府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was promoted to prefect of Huangzhou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was made prefect of Huangzhou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 甫蒞任，而張亮基調湖南，奏調豐玉往襄軍事，助守長沙。

translations.literal: He had barely taken office when Zhang Liangji was transferred to Hunan and memorialized to call Fengyu to assist with military affairs at Xiang and help defend Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken office when Zhang Liangji was sent to Hunan and had Fengyu called up to help with the war effort and the defense of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 尋從總督徐廣縉赴岳州，武昌已陷，豐玉請廣縉速移鎮黃州，截賊下竄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Governor-General Xu Guangjin to Yuezhou; Wuchang had already fallen, and Fengyu asked Guangjin to move his headquarters quickly to Huangzhou to cut off the rebels' descent downstream.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Governor-General Xu Guangjin to Yuezhou. Wuchang had already fallen, and Fengyu urged Guangjin to shift his headquarters quickly to Huangzhou to block the rebels moving downriver.

sentences.zh: 廣縉不能用，得罪去，張亮基代之。

translations.literal: Guangjin could not adopt the plan, offended and departed, and Zhang Liangji replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin would not follow the advice, left office under disgrace, and Zhang Liangji replaced him.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢湖北督糧道，署漢黃德道。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to grain transport commissioner of Hubei and acted as intendant of the Han, Huang, and De circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Hubei's grain transport commissioner and acted as intendant of the Han-Huang-De circuit.

sentences.zh: 廣濟民變，戕縣令。

translations.literal: The people of Guangji mutinied and killed the county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Guangji rose in revolt and killed the county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 黃州知府邵綸及新令鮑開運往撫，均遇害。

translations.literal: The Huangzhou prefect Shao Lun and the newly appointed magistrate Bao Kaiyun went to pacify them and were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou Prefect Shao Lun and the newly appointed magistrate Bao Kaiyun went to pacify the crowd and were both killed.

sentences.zh: 豐玉偕按察使江忠源往剿，捕斬數百人，乃定。

translations.literal: Fengyu went with the provincial judicial commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan to suppress them, captured and executed several hundred men, and only then was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu went with Provincial Judicial Commissioner Jiang Zhongyuan to suppress the revolt, captured and executed several hundred men, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 會粵匪由江寧分竄上游，忠源率師援江西，亮基令豐玉統湖北防軍駐田家鎮。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Guangdong rebels from Jiangning split and fled upriver; Zhongyuan led troops to aid Jiangxi, and Liangji ordered Fengyu to command the Hubei defense army stationed at Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong rebels then split from Nanjing and raided upriver. Zhongyuan marched to aid Jiangxi, and Liangji put Fengyu in command of Hubei's defensive forces at Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 鎮當江北岸，後有大山曰黃金塔，小山曰磨盤，下有河直入江中，與南岸半壁山接。

translations.literal: The town stood on the north bank of the Yangzi; behind it was a great mountain called Golden Pagoda and a lesser one called Millstone; below was a river flowing straight into the Yangzi, opposite Banbishan on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: The town lay on the north bank of the Yangzi. Behind it stood Golden Pagoda Mountain and the smaller Millstone Hill; a river ran straight into the Yangzi opposite Banbishan on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 山塹水湍，舟行必循湍繞河乃得過，最據形勢。

translations.literal: The mountains formed a barrier and the water ran swift; boats had to follow the rapids and circle the river to pass—it was the most commanding position.
translations.idiomatic: Steep mountains and swift water forced boats to thread the rapids around the river mouth, making it the strongest choke point on the route.

sentences.zh: 豐玉列營諸山，於河上聯筏作城，列砲以守。

translations.literal: Fengyu arrayed camps on the mountains, linked rafts on the river to form a wall, and lined up cannon to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu camped his men on the hills, chained rafts into a floating wall across the river, and lined up artillery.

sentences.zh: 半壁山背倚湖，湖通興國，入湖處曰富池口。

translations.literal: Banbishan backed onto a lake that connected with Xingguo; the lake's entrance was called Fuchi Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Banbishan backed onto a lake linked to Xingguo; the lake entrance was Fuchi Mouth.

sentences.zh: 豐玉欲分營半壁山上而兵單，僅遣兵弁瞭望而已。

translations.literal: Fengyu wished to divide camps on Banbishan but his troops were few, and he sent only officers to keep watch.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu wanted to post troops on Banbishan but had too few men and sent only officers to keep watch.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊由南昌退九江，遂上犯田家鎮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the rebels retreated from Nanchang to Jiujiang and then moved upriver to attack Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rebels fell back from Nanchang to Jiujiang and then struck upstream at Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 豐玉偕總兵楊昌泗憑牆砲擊沉賊船，又斃陸路撲營賊，乘勝追壓乃退。

translations.literal: Fengyu with Regional Commander Yang Changsi used the wall batteries to sink rebel boats, also killed rebels who charged the camps by land, pursued with the advantage gained, and pressed them back.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu and Regional Commander Yang Changsi used the river batteries to sink rebel boats, killed rebels who stormed the camps overland, and drove them back in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 次日，賊船擁至，分三路迎擊，斃賊甚眾，毀其大船。

translations.literal: The next day rebel boats crowded in; he met them on three fronts, killed very many rebels, and destroyed their large vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a mass of rebel boats arrived. He met them on three fronts, killed large numbers, and destroyed their largest ships.

sentences.zh: 賊由富池口分船數百犯興國，會江忠源由江西回援，賊復由興國會於富池口。

translations.literal: The rebels sent several hundred boats from Fuchi Mouth to attack Xingguo; meanwhile Jiang Zhongyuan returned from Jiangxi to reinforce, and the rebels gathered again from Xingguo at Fuchi Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent hundreds of boats from Fuchi Mouth against Xingguo. Jiang Zhongyuan returned from Jiangxi to reinforce, and the rebels regrouped at Fuchi Mouth from Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 荊門知州李榞輕軍襲之，豐玉遣兵夾擊，敗挫，榞陣歿。

translations.literal: Jingmen Prefect Li Yuan led a light force to raid them; Fengyu sent troops to attack from both sides; they were defeated and checked, and Yuan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmen Prefect Li Yuan led a light force in a raid. Fengyu sent troops to hit them from both sides, but the attack failed and Yuan was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 忠源聞田家鎮危急，調九江兵馳援，未達，忠源獨挈親兵數十人至。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan heard Tianjiazhen was critical, ordered Jiujiang troops to hurry to aid, but they did not arrive; Zhongyuan alone brought several dozen personal soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Tianjiazhen was in peril, Zhongyuan ordered troops from Jiujiang to rush to the rescue, but they did not arrive in time; he came alone with a few dozen personal guards.

sentences.zh: 見賊眾兵單，驚曰：「不可守矣！」

translations.literal: Seeing the rebels numerous and his troops few, he exclaimed in alarm, "It cannot be held!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how many rebels there were and how few defenders he had, he cried in alarm, "This place cannot be held!"

sentences.zh: 次晨，大風作，賊連檣驟至，環撲我營。

translations.literal: The next morning a great wind arose; rebel boats with linked masts arrived suddenly and surrounded and assaulted our camps.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning a strong wind blew up. Rebel boats with linked masts surged in and surrounded the camps on every side.

sentences.zh: 豐玉偕漢黃德道張汝瀛督戰，筏城被焚，營壘皆不守。

translations.literal: Fengyu with Zhang Ruying, intendant of Han, Huang, and De, directed the battle; the raft wall was burned and the camps could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu and Han-Huang-De Intendant Zhang Ruying directed the defense, but the raft wall was burned and every camp gave way.

sentences.zh: 豐玉手佩刀殺賊，遂自剄，汝瀛同殉焉。

translations.literal: Fengyu with his own hand and wearing sword killed rebels, then cut his own throat; Ruying died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyu drew his sword and killed rebels with his own hand, then cut his throat; Ruying died at his side.

sentences.zh: 忠源親隨僅存數人，收集餘眾，退駐廣濟。

translations.literal: Of Zhongyuan's personal followers only a few remained; he gathered the remaining troops and withdrew to station at Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: Only a handful of Zhongyuan's personal guards survived. He rallied the remnants and fell back to Guangji.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, his family was granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，大學士李鴻章疏陳豐玉政績、死事狀，予諡勇烈，建專祠。

translations.literal: During Guangxu, Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang memorialized Fengyu's administrative achievements and the circumstances of his death, and he was given the posthumous title Yonglie and a dedicated shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign, Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang described Fengyu's record in office and his death in battle; he was given the posthumous title Yonglie and a dedicated shrine was built.

sentences.zh: 張汝瀛，山東樂陵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ruying was a native of Leling in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ruying was from Leling in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道光元年舉人。

translations.literal: He was a provincial graduate in the first year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He received his provincial degree in the first year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 官廣西知縣，歷貴縣、蒼梧，以剿匪功洊升知府，亦為張亮基所薦拔。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate in Guangxi, passing through Guixian and Cangwu; for merit in suppressing bandits he was repeatedly promoted to prefect, and he too was advanced by Zhang Liangji.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a magistrate in Guangxi at Guixian and Cangwu, was promoted step by step to prefect for suppressing bandits, and was likewise advanced by Zhang Liangji.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，擢漢黃德道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was promoted to intendant of Han, Huang, and De.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was made intendant of the Han-Huang-De circuit.

sentences.zh: 甫抵任，偕豐玉同守田家鎮，歿於陣，予騎都尉世職，追諡勇節。

translations.literal: He had barely reached his post when he joined Fengyu in defending Tianjiazhen, died in battle, was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and posthumously given the title Yongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken office when he joined Fengyu in defending Tianjiazhen, fell in battle, and was granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry with the posthumous title Yongjie.

sentences.zh: 金雲門，安徽休寧人。

translations.literal: Jin Yunmen was a native of Xiuning in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yunmen was from Xiuning in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年進士，官浙江雲和知縣。

translations.literal: He was a metropolitan graduate in the thirteenth year of Daoguang and served as magistrate of Yunhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in the thirteenth year of Daoguang and served as magistrate of Yunhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 改湖北，歷天門、崇陽、隨州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hubei and served successively at Tianmen, Chongyang, and Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hubei, he served at Tianmen, Chongyang, and Suizhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 以擒崇陽匪首鍾人傑功，晉知州。

translations.literal: For capturing the Chongyang bandit chief Zhong Renjie he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing the Chongyang bandit chief Zhong Renjie he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 洊擢安陸知府，署糧儲道，護按察使，調署黃州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Anlu, acted as grain storage commissioner, protected the provincial judicial commissioner, and was transferred to act at Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to prefect of Anlu, acted as grain storage commissioner and provincial judicial commissioner, and was transferred to act at Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自田家鎮失利，賊遂進陷黃州，雲門死之，贈太僕寺卿，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Tianjiazhen the rebels advanced and took Huangzhou; Yunmen died there, was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Tianjiazhen the rebels pressed on and took Huangzhou; Yunmen died in the fighting, was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and his family received the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後京山士民以政績卓越請建祠，諡果毅。

translations.literal: Later the gentry and people of Jingshan requested a shrine for his outstanding administration, and he was given the posthumous title Guoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Later the gentry and people of Jingshan asked for a shrine in recognition of his outstanding administration, and he received the posthumous title Guoyi.

sentences.zh: 唐樹義，貴州遵義人。

translations.literal: Tang Shuyi was a native of Zunyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shuyi was from Zunyi in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十一年舉人，官湖北咸豐、監利、江夏知縣，洊擢湖北布政使。

translations.literal: He was a provincial graduate in the twenty-first year of Jiaqing, served as magistrate at Xianfeng, Jianli, and Jiangxia in Hubei, and was repeatedly promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of the twenty-first year of Jiaqing, he served as magistrate at Xianfeng, Jianli, and Jiangxia in Hubei and rose to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以病歸，在籍辦團練。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of illness and organized local militia training in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Illness sent him home, where he organized local militia in his native district.

sentences.zh: 張亮基奏調湖北，署按察使。

translations.literal: Zhang Liangji memorialized to transfer him to Hubei, and he acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liangji had him called to Hubei, where he acted as provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及田家鎮軍事亟，率兵防江北陵路，駐廣濟。

translations.literal: When military affairs at Tianjiazhen grew urgent, he led troops to defend the Jiangbei Ling route and was stationed at Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: When the fighting at Tianjiazhen grew desperate, he led troops to guard the Jiangbei Ling route and camped at Guangji.

sentences.zh: 既而黃州、漢陽相繼陷，樹義勦賊德安，進軍灄口。

translations.literal: Before long Huangzhou and Hanyang fell in succession; Shuyi suppressed bandits at De'an and advanced his army to Shankou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangzhou and Hanyang soon fell in turn. Shuyi fought bandits at De'an and advanced to Shankou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，戰失利，褫職留任，率舟師禦賊金口，船破，死之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng battle went against him; he was stripped of rank but kept at his post, led a naval force to resist rebels at Jinkou, his boats were broken, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he was beaten in battle, stripped of rank but kept on duty, led a flotilla against the rebels at Jinkou, lost his ships, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉世職，諡威恪。

translations.literal: He was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry and given the posthumous title Weike.
translations.idiomatic: His family received the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous title Weike.

sentences.zh: 岳興阿，博爾濟吉特氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Yue Xing'a, of the Borjigit clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xing'a, of the Borjigit clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 考授內閣中書，出為河南南陽知府，洊擢湖北布政使。

translations.literal: Through examination he was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat, went out as prefect of Nanyang in Henan, and was repeatedly promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: By examination he entered the Grand Secretariat as a secretary, became prefect of Nanyang in Henan, and rose to provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 四年，武昌陷，死之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wuchang fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wuchang fell and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 予騎都尉世職，諡剛節。

translations.literal: He was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry and given the posthumous title Gangjie.
translations.idiomatic: His family received the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous title Gangjie.

sentences.zh: 易容之，廣東鶴山人。

translations.literal: Yi Rongzhi was a native of Heshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Rongzhi was from Heshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 捐納銓授湖北德安知府。

translations.literal: He purchased an office and through selection was appointed prefect of De'an in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He bought an office and was appointed prefect of De'an in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 四年，德安陷，罵賊死之，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year De'an fell; he cursed the rebels and died, and was granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year De'an fell; he cursed the rebels and was killed, and his family received the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李榞自有傳。

translations.literal: Li Yuan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: =溫紹原=溫紹原，字北屏，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: = Wen Shaoyuan = Wen Shaoyuan, styled Beiping, was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shaoyuan, styled Beiping, was from Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 少負奇略。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed unusual strategic talent.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth he showed uncommon strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 入貲為兩淮鹽運司經歷，改知縣。

translations.literal: He contributed funds to become secretary of the Liang-Huai Salt Transport Commission and was later changed to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased an office as secretary of the Liang-Huai Salt Transport Commission and later became a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，署六合，減賦役，蠲苛法，民戴之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he acted at Liuhe, reduced taxes and corvée, abolished harsh regulations, and the people revered him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Liuhe, cut taxes and labor levies, repealed harsh rules, and won the people's devotion.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陷武昌東下，紹原以六合為南北要衝，勸民積穀儲群堡，修城垣，治守具。

translations.literal: When the Guangdong rebels took Wuchang and marched east, Shaoyuan regarded Liuhe as the vital passage between north and south, urged the people to store grain and stock the clustered forts, repaired the walls, and prepared defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels took Wuchang and marched east, Shaoyuan saw Liuhe as the key link between north and south. He urged the people to store grain, stock the local forts, repair the walls, and ready the defenses.

sentences.zh: 團練四鄉，合為一氣，別募壯勇訓練。

translations.literal: He trained militia in the four townships until they acted as one body, and separately recruited stalwart braves for drill.
translations.idiomatic: He organized militia in the four townships into a single force and separately recruited and trained stalwart volunteers.

sentences.zh: 三年春，江寧陷，賊遊騎至境，輒殲之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Jiangning fell; when rebel scouting horsemen reached the border he destroyed them at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Nanjing fell; whenever rebel scouting parties reached his border he wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 既而大至，禦於龍池，以兵單失利，練總徐琳、達成榮戰死，紹原退保南關。

translations.literal: Before long they came in force; he defended at Longchi, but with few troops suffered defeat; militia leaders Xu Lin and Da Chengrong died in battle, and Shaoyuan withdrew to hold the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a larger force arrived. He met them at Longchi but was beaten for lack of numbers; militia leaders Xu Lin and Da Chengrong were killed, and Shaoyuan fell back to defend the south gate.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，賊營火，乘亂攻之，斬偽丞相一、偽統制四，餘眾殲焉。

translations.literal: As dusk fell the rebel camp caught fire; he took advantage of the disorder to attack, beheaded one false chancellor and four false commanders, and annihilated the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the rebel camp caught fire. He attacked in the confusion, killed one false chancellor and four false commanders, and wiped out the rest.

sentences.zh: 紹原益增守要隘，浚品字坑伏地雷。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan further strengthened defense of critical passes and dug pin-shaped pits to conceal land mines.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyuan strengthened the defenses at key passes and dug pin-shaped pits for concealed land mines.

sentences.zh: 守備秦淮陽，千總夏定邦、王家幹，皆能戰，賊屢至，隨機御之，每擒斬過當，賊懼之，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Qin Huaiyang and the company commanders Xia Dingbang and Wang Jiangan were all able fighters; whenever rebels came he met them as circumstances required, each time capturing and killing more than his due share; the rebels feared him and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Commander Qin Huaiyang and company commanders Xia Dingbang and Wang Jiangan were all capable fighters. Rebels came repeatedly, and he met each attack as circumstances required, killing more than his share each time until they feared him and would not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣向榮、總督怡良先後上其功，以知府升用，賜花翎，特詔嘉獎；

translations.literal: The imperial commissioner Xiang Rong and the governor Yiliang successively reported his merit; he was promoted for use as prefect, granted the peacock feather, and specially edicted for praise;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Xiang Rong and Governor Yiliang reported his achievements in turn. He was promoted to prefect, given the peacock feather, and honored by special edict;

sentences.zh: 並以紳民深明大義，蠲免六合一年丁漕，增廣學額，以示旌異。

translations.literal: and because the gentry and people deeply understood the greater duty, one year's land tax and grain transport levies for Liuhe were remitted and the quota of students at the examinations was increased, to show special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: and because the local gentry and people had shown such public spirit, Liuhe's land tax and grain transport levies were remitted for one year and its examination quota was increased as a mark of special honor.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊屯九洑洲，結簰置砲，翼以戰艦，順流下，至八卦洲，紹原夜以小舟襲之，縱火焚簰幾盡，偕總兵武慶、江浦知縣曾勉禮，分路進攻九洑洲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the rebels encamped at Jiufuzhou, linked rafts and set cannon, supported by warships, and drifted downstream to Baguazhou; Shaoyuan at night with small boats raided them and set fires that burned the rafts nearly all; together with Regional Commander Wu Qing and Jiangpu Magistrate Zeng Mianli he attacked Jiufuzhou by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the rebels camped at Jiufuzhou, chained rafts together with artillery, and moved downstream under cover of warships to Baguazhou. Shaoyuan raided them at night in small boats and burned nearly all the rafts, then joined Regional Commander Wu Qing and Jiangpu Magistrate Zeng Mianli in a multi-pronged assault on Jiufuzhou.

sentences.zh: 天大霧，架浮橋襲賊營，大破之，平其壘，被議敘。

translations.literal: Heavy fog covered the sky; they built a pontoon bridge and stormed the rebel camp, inflicting a great defeat and leveling their fortifications, and he was recommended for reward.
translations.idiomatic: In heavy fog they threw a pontoon bridge across and stormed the rebel camp, routing the enemy and leveling their fortifications, and he was recommended for promotion.

sentences.zh: 五年，署江寧知府，在縣設治，督辦府屬團練事宜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he acted as prefect of Jiangning, established his administration in the county, and supervised militia affairs throughout the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he acted as prefect of Jiangning, set up his office in the county, and oversaw militia training throughout the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊屢糾悍黨自浦口來撲，皆不得逞。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly gathered fierce bands from Pukou to assault him, but none could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels repeatedly rallied fierce bands from Pukou to attack him, but none succeeded.

sentences.zh: 六年，大軍攻鎮江、瓜洲急，賊數路來援。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the main army pressed the attack on Zhenjiang and Guazhou urgently, and the rebels came to relieve them by several routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the main army pressed hard against Zhenjiang and Guazhou, and the rebels sent relief forces by several routes.

sentences.zh: 其自蕪湖來者，紹原要之於江，七戰皆捷，進劃南岸七里洲賊壘，毀其舟。

translations.literal: Those coming from Wuhu he intercepted on the river; in seven battles he was victorious each time, advanced to cut the rebel fortifications at Qilizhou on the south bank, and destroyed their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Those coming from Wuhu he intercepted on the river and won seven battles in a row. He then advanced against the rebel fort at Qilizhou on the south bank and destroyed their boats.

sentences.zh: 賊乃出陸路，竄踞高資港、下蜀街，巡撫吉爾杭阿檄紹原赴援。

translations.literal: The rebels then moved by land, fled to occupy Gaozigang and Xiashu Street, and Governor Jirhang'a ordered Shaoyuan to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then moved overland and seized Gaozigang and Xiashu Street. Governor Jirhang'a ordered Shaoyuan to reinforce the position.

sentences.zh: 紹原令其弟溫綸率千人往戰，數有功。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan ordered his younger brother Wen Lun to lead a thousand men into battle, and he won merit several times.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyuan sent his younger brother Wen Lun with a thousand men and won several victories.

sentences.zh: 江北托明阿軍潰，揚州陷。

translations.literal: To Ming'a's army north of the Yangzi collapsed, and Yangzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: To Ming'a's army north of the Yangzi collapsed and Yangzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 紹原由儀徵往援，而賊陷江浦，犯浦口，踞六合葛塘集，偕張國樑馳擊於龍池，大破之；

translations.literal: Shaoyuan went from Yizheng to reinforce, but the rebels took Jiangpu, attacked Pukou, and occupied Getangji in Liuhe; together with Zhang Guoliang he hurried to strike them at Longchi and inflicted a great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyuan marched from Yizheng to reinforce, but the rebels took Jiangpu, struck Pukou, and seized Getangji in Liuhe. He and Zhang Guoliang rushed to attack them at Longchi and routed them;

sentences.zh: 又破之於盤城集，連复江浦、浦口。

translations.literal: defeated them again at Panchengji, and in succession recovered Jiangpu and Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: defeated them again at Panchengji, and recovered Jiangpu and Pukou in succession.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，擢道員。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was promoted to intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he was promoted to intendant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊再陷江浦，進犯六合，紹原合水陸擊走之。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels again took Jiangpu and advanced to attack Liuhe; Shaoyuan combined land and water forces and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels took Jiangpu again and advanced on Liuhe. Shaoyuan combined land and river forces and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 時軍事分隸江南、江北兩大營。

translations.literal: At that time military affairs were divided under the two great camps of Jiangnan and Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs were then divided between the Jiangnan and Jiangbei command camps.

sentences.zh: 六合地居江北，紹原以孤城為保障，且數出境渡江助大軍攻剿立功，向榮深推重，令充南軍翼長。

translations.literal: Liuhe lay north of the Yangzi; Shaoyuan used his isolated city as a bulwark and repeatedly crossed the border and the river to aid the main army in attack and suppression, winning merit; Xiang Rong deeply esteemed him and ordered him to serve as wing commander of the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe lay north of the Yangzi. Shaoyuan held his isolated city as a bastion and repeatedly crossed the river to help the main army win victories. Xiang Rong held him in high regard and made him wing commander of the southern army.

sentences.zh: 德興阿督北軍，意嗛之。

translations.literal: De Xing'a commanded the northern army and resented him inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a commanded the northern army and resented him.

sentences.zh: 七年，天長、來安土匪起，遣兵破之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year bandits rose at Tianchang and Lai'an; he sent troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year bandits rose at Tianchang and Lai'an; he sent troops and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 列上所部戰績，德興阿謂越境邀功，置勿錄，紹原力爭，遂以乾頂保舉疏劾褫職，仍留六合帶勇防堵。

translations.literal: He listed the battle achievements of his command; De Xing'a said he had crossed borders to claim merit and set the record aside; Shaoyuan argued forcefully, and thereupon through a memorial of recommendation and impeachment with a dry topknot he was stripped of office but remained at Liuhe leading braves in defense.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a list of his unit's victories. De Xing'a dismissed it as border-crossing self-promotion and refused to record it. Shaoyuan protested fiercely, and De Xing'a impeached him and stripped him of rank, though he was left at Liuhe to lead defensive forces.

sentences.zh: 尋有旨命兼管江寧、江浦團練。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to take joint charge of militia in Jiangning and Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict put him in joint charge of militia in Jiangning and Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 總督何桂清疏言：「紹原以一縣倡募水陸各勇，激勵紳團，屢殲賊眾，出奇制勝。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Guiqing memorialized: "Shaoyuan from a single county initiated recruitment of land and water braves alike, roused the gentry militia, repeatedly annihilated rebel forces, and won by unexpected stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Guiqing wrote: "From a single county Shaoyuan raised land and river forces, rallied the gentry militia, repeatedly destroyed rebel bands, and won by bold stratagems.

sentences.zh: 且餘力上搤江浦，下救儀徵，北援來安，江北大營得免西顧之憂。

translations.literal: Moreover with his surplus strength he blocked Jiangpu above, rescued Yizheng below, aided Lai'an to the north, and the Jiangbei great camp was spared worry over its western flank.
translations.idiomatic: With his spare strength he held Jiangpu upstream, relieved Yizheng downstream, aided Lai'an to the north, and spared the Jiangbei camp worry about its western flank.

sentences.zh: 自來安至廬州，尚有一線運道可通者，亦惟紹原是賴。

translations.literal: From Lai'an to Luzhou, where a single thread of transport route could still be kept open, reliance was also only on Shaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The slender supply line that still connected Lai'an with Luzhou depended on him alone.

sentences.zh: 才足匡時如紹原者，實不多見。

translations.literal: Men of talent sufficient to aid the age like Shaoyuan are truly seldom seen.
translations.idiomatic: Men of his talent, able to steady the times, are truly rare.

sentences.zh: 請復原官，以維繫眾心。」

translations.literal: I request restoration of his original office to bind the hearts of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that his former rank be restored to keep the people's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 詔允開復知府。

translations.literal: An edict approved restoration to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his restoration to prefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，從大軍克來安，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the main army in capturing Lai'an and was given the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the main army in taking Lai'an and received the brevet rank of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 悍酋李秀成、陳玉成大舉援江寧，先陷江浦。

translations.literal: The fierce chiefs Li Xiucheng and Chen Yucheng led a great force to relieve Jiangning and first took Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chiefs Li Xiucheng and Chen Yucheng marched in force to relieve Nanjing and first took Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 德興阿退六合，三戰皆敗，又退揚州。

translations.literal: De Xing'a withdrew from Liuhe, was defeated in three battles, and withdrew again to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a fell back from Liuhe, lost three battles in a row, and retreated to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊久憾紹原，合力圍攻。

translations.literal: The rebels had long resented Shaoyuan and joined forces to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long hated Shaoyuan and joined forces to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 文宗恐其有失，詔促德興阿、勝保速援，皆不至。

translations.literal: Wenzong feared he might be lost and edicted De Xing'a and Sheng Bao to hurry to his aid, but neither arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong feared for his safety and ordered De Xing'a and Sheng Bao to rush to his relief, but neither came.

sentences.zh: 紹原堅守幾及一月，力竭城陷，死之。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan held firm for nearly a month; his strength exhausted, the city fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyuan held out for nearly a month, but his strength gave out, the city fell, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 張國樑既克揚州，即日馳赴，於城陷次日始至，聞者莫不嗟悼。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang, having taken Yangzhou, hurried there the same day, but arrived only on the day after the city fell; all who heard sighed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang, having taken Yangzhou, rushed to the rescue the same day but arrived only the day after the city fell. All who heard of it mourned.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉紹原「六載守城，久為江北重鎮。

translations.literal: An edict praised Shaoyuan: "For six years he defended the city, long the great stronghold of Jiangbei.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Shaoyuan: "For six years he held the city, long the great bastion of the north bank.

sentences.zh: 援師未集，力竭捐軀，深為憫惜」，贈布政使銜，予騎都尉世職，於六合建專祠，諡壯勇。

translations.literal: Relief troops did not gather; his strength exhausted, he gave his life—a matter of deep compassion," granted the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner, the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, a dedicated shrine at Liuhe, and the posthumous title Zhuangyong.
translations.idiomatic: Relief never arrived; exhausted, he gave his life—a loss deeply lamented." He was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner, the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, a memorial shrine at Liuhe, and the posthumous title Zhuangyong.

sentences.zh: 夏定邦，六合人；

translations.literal: Xia Dingbang was a native of Liuhe;
translations.idiomatic: Xia Dingbang was from Liuhe;

sentences.zh: 王家幹，睢寧人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiangan was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiangan was from Suining.

sentences.zh: 從紹原守禦，及八卦洲、九洑洲、江浦諸戰，皆有殊績，並擢官都司。

translations.literal: They followed Shaoyuan in defense and in the battles at Baguazhou, Jiufuzhou, Jiangpu, and elsewhere all won unusual merit, and both were promoted to the rank of brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: They fought under Shaoyuan in the defenses and at Baguazhou, Jiufuzhou, Jiangpu, and other battles, winning distinction each time, and both were promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 城陷，同死難。

translations.literal: When the city fell they died together in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell they died with him.

sentences.zh: =金光箸=金光箸，字濂石，直隸天津人。

translations.literal: = Jin Guangzhu = Jin Guangzhu, styled Lianshi, was a native of Tianjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guangzhu, styled Lianshi, was from Tianjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 捐納通判，分甘肅，署巴燕戎格廳，改安徽知縣。

translations.literal: He purchased the office of subprefect, was assigned to Gansu, acted at the Bayan Rongge subprefecture, and was transferred to magistrate in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He bought the office of subprefect, served in Gansu as acting head of Bayan Rongge, and was transferred to a magistracy in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 青陽民因歲荒抗徵，幾釀變，光箸奉檄單騎諭解之。

translations.literal: The people of Qingyang resisted tax collection because of famine and nearly provoked an uprising; Guangzhu received orders and went alone on horseback to persuade and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qingyang resisted tax collection during a famine and nearly rose in revolt. Guangzhu went alone on horseback under orders and talked them down.

sentences.zh: 補建平，調定遠。

translations.literal: He was appointed to Jianping and transferred to Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Jianping and transferred to Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 定遠多盜，巡緝無間，捕土匪陳小喚子置之法。

translations.literal: Dingyuan had many bandits; he patrolled and searched without pause, captured the bandit Chen Xiaohuanzi, and put him to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan was full of bandits. He patrolled relentlessly, captured the outlaw Chen Xiaohuanzi, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 又調壽州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年春，粵匪連陷安慶、江寧，皖北盜蜂起，光箸集民團備戰守。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Xianfeng the Guangdong rebels successively took Anqing and Jiangning; bandits swarmed in northern Anhui, and Guangzhu gathered militia to prepare for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Xianfeng the rebels took Anqing and Nanjing in succession, banditry erupted across northern Anhui, and Guangzhu rallied militia for defense.

sentences.zh: 陸遐齡者，定遠巨猾，係安慶獄。

translations.literal: Lu Xialing was a great villain of Dingyuan, held in Anqing prison.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xialing was a notorious outlaw of Dingyuan who had been held in the Anqing jail.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊令歸結黨為北路應，擾定遠、壽州、合肥，勢甚張。

translations.literal: When the city fell the rebels ordered him to return and rally followers as northern-route support; he harassed Dingyuan, Shouzhou, and Hefei, and his power grew very great.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the rebels sent him home to rally men as their northern wing. He raided Dingyuan, Shouzhou, and Hefei, and his power grew rapidly.

sentences.zh: 巡撫週天爵兵少不能制，令光箸圖之。

translations.literal: Governor Zhou Tianjue had too few troops to control him and ordered Guangzhu to deal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhou Tianjue had too few troops to control him and ordered Guangzhu to eliminate him.

sentences.zh: 先布間諜，散其黨羽，然後進攻莊木橋。

translations.literal: First he deployed spies to scatter his followers, then advanced to attack Zhuangmuqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent spies to break up Xialing's band, then attacked Zhuangmuqiao.

sentences.zh: 光箸設奇計，親率勇士擒遐齡父子及其黨四十餘人，戮之。

translations.literal: Guangzhu devised a stratagem, personally led stalwart warriors to capture Xialing father and son and more than forty of their followers, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhu laid a stratagem, led picked warriors in person, captured Xialing and his son along with more than forty followers, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 天爵特疏薦，晉秩知府，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Tianjue specially memorialized to recommend him; he was promoted in rank to prefect and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue specially recommended him to court. He was promoted to prefect and given the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊由江寧、揚州分股北竄臨淮，擾及鳳陽、懷遠。

translations.literal: In the fourth month rebels from Jiangning and Yangzhou split into columns and fled north to Linhuai, disturbing Fengyang and Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month rebels from Nanjing and Yangzhou split into columns, fled north to Linhuai, and raided Fengyang and Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光箸於兩河口立水營，八公山雜張旗幟為疑兵，列砲要隘。

translations.literal: Guangzhu established a naval camp at Lianghekou, on Bagongshan set out mixed banners as decoy troops, and lined cannon at critical passes.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhu set up a naval camp at Lianghekou, planted decoy banners on Bagong Mountain, and posted artillery at the key passes.

sentences.zh: 獲賊諜逃兵，並斬之以徇，壽州獲安。

translations.literal: He captured rebel spies and deserters and beheaded them all to display as warning; Shouzhou was secured.
translations.idiomatic: He captured rebel spies and deserters, executed them publicly, and secured Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊復由六合撲正陽關，光箸調練勇千​​，屯三十里鋪及兩河口迎擊，殲賊二百餘人，乃引去。

translations.literal: In the fifth month rebels again from Liuhe rushed Zhengyang Pass; Guangzhu mobilized a thousand trained braves, encamped at the Thirty-Li Station and Lianghekou to meet them, annihilated more than two hundred rebels, and they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rebels from Liuhe struck Zhengyang Pass again. Guangzhu mobilized a thousand trained volunteers, posted them at the Thirty-Li Station and Lianghekou, killed more than two hundred rebels, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 招降附近土匪談家寶、張茂等黨眾數千，皆效用。

translations.literal: He induced the surrender of nearby bandits Tan Jiabao, Zhang Mao, and others with several thousand followers, and all came to serve.
translations.idiomatic: He induced nearby bandits Tan Jiabao, Zhang Mao, and others with several thousand followers to surrender, and all entered his service.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，粵匪陷廬州。

translations.literal: That winter the Guangdong rebels took Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels took Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，六安繼陷，北路捻匪日猖獗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Lu'an fell in succession, and Nian bandits on the northern route grew daily more rampant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Lu'an fell in turn, and Nian bandits on the northern route grew bolder by the day.

sentences.zh: 和春督大軍規廬州，不暇北顧。

translations.literal: He Chun directed the main army in planning against Luzhou and had no leisure to look north.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun led the main army against Luzhou and could not spare attention for the north.

sentences.zh: 袁甲三剿捻，徬徨於皖、豫之交。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiasan suppressed the Nian, hesitating at the border of Anhui and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiasan fought the Nian but wavered along the Anhui-Henan border.

sentences.zh: 正陽為要衝，距州城六十里。

translations.literal: Zhengyang was a critical pass, sixty li from the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyang was the critical pass, sixty li from the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 光箸扼關以御，捻黨數來犯，五戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Guangzhu held the pass to resist; Nian bands came to attack several times, and in five battles he was victorious each time.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhu held the pass against them. Nian bands attacked repeatedly, and he won five battles in a row.

sentences.zh: 季學盛踞於家圍，而馬四、馬五、王亮彩、鄧三虎等諸捻黨出沒州境，先後平之。

translations.literal: Ji Xuesheng occupied Jiawei, while Ma Si, Ma Wu, Wang Liangcai, Deng Sanhu, and other Nian bands ranged within the prefecture; he pacified them one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xuesheng held Jiawei, while Ma Si, Ma Wu, Wang Liangcai, Deng Sanhu, and other Nian leaders raided the prefecture. Guangzhu suppressed them one after another.

sentences.zh: 廬州大軍無後顧憂者，光箸之力也。

translations.literal: That the Luzhou main army had no worry over its rear was due to Guangzhu's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Luzhou army's freedom from worry about its rear was Guangzhu's doing.

sentences.zh: 五年，大軍克廬州，光箸署知府，撫流亡，嚴斥候，數殲伏匪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the main army took Luzhou; Guangzhu acted as prefect, comforted the displaced, tightened scouts, and repeatedly destroyed hidden bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the main army took Luzhou. Guangzhu acted as prefect, resettled refugees, tightened scouting, and repeatedly destroyed hidden bandits.

sentences.zh: 六年，遂實授。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he received a regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋巡撫福濟疏列其治行上聞，以道員記名，署廬鳳道。

translations.literal: Soon Governor Fuiji memorialized listing his administrative conduct for report to the throne; he was noted by name for intendant and acted as intendant of the Lu and Feng circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Governor Fuiji reported his record in office to court. He was marked for promotion to intendant and acted as intendant of the Lu-Feng circuit.

sentences.zh: 時和春移督江南大軍，袁甲三再起軍臨淮，捻勢南趨。

translations.literal: At that time He Chun was transferred to command the Jiangnan main army, Yuan Jiasan again raised troops at Linhuai, and Nian power pressed south.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was then transferred to command the Jiangnan army, Yuan Jiasan raised troops again at Linhuai, and Nian forces pressed south.

sentences.zh: 光箸甫出兵，捻首張洛行已破周鎮、王莊，犯三十里鋪。

translations.literal: Guangzhu had barely marched out when the Nian chief Zhang Luoxing had already broken Zhouzhen and Wangzhuang and attacked the Thirty-Li Station.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhu had barely marched out when Nian chief Zhang Luoxing had already taken Zhouzhen and Wangzhuang and was striking the Thirty-Li Station.

sentences.zh: 光箸背水為陣，令曰：「有進無退！」

translations.literal: Guangzhu formed battle lines with water at his back and ordered: "Advance only, no retreat!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhu drew up his line with water at his back and ordered, "Forward only—no retreat!"

sentences.zh: 分三路擊之，以八百人破賊數万。

translations.literal: He attacked on three routes and with eight hundred men broke tens of thousands of rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked on three fronts and with eight hundred men routed tens of thousands of rebels.

sentences.zh: 七年春，捻匪龔德等掠正陽關，光箸偕副都統德勒格爾渡河襲擊，斃賊八百餘，追七十里。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Nian bandits Gong De and others plundered Zhengyang Pass; Guangzhu with Vice Commander-in-Chief Deleger crossed the river to raid them, killed more than eight hundred rebels, and pursued seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year Nian bandits led by Gong De raided Zhengyang Pass. Guangzhu crossed the river with Vice Commander-in-Chief Deleger, killed more than eight hundred rebels, and pursued them seventy li.

sentences.zh: 將搗其巢，聞六安​​復為粵匪所陷，回保壽州。

translations.literal: About to strike their nest, he heard Lu'an had again been taken by Guangdong rebels and returned to defend Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to strike their base when word came that Lu'an had fallen again to the rebels, and he turned back to defend Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 粵匪驟至，圍城。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels arrived suddenly and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels arrived suddenly and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 破其地雷，夜乘霧出城，分三路襲賊營，鄉團應之。

translations.literal: He destroyed their land mines, at night took advantage of fog to leave the city, attacked rebel camps on three routes, and local militia responded.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed their mines, slipped out under cover of night fog, struck the rebel camps on three fronts, and local militia joined in.

sentences.zh: 賊驚潰，追擊，斃賊千餘，圍立解。

translations.literal: The rebels fled in alarm; he pursued, killed more than a thousand rebels, and the siege was at once lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke in panic. He pursued, killed more than a thousand, and the siege was lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 捷入，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was given the brevet rank of provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he received the brevet rank of provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乘勝合水陸進剿，毀賊營四十餘處，克正陽關，賜號鏗色巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Pressing the advantage he combined land and water forces in pursuit, destroyed more than forty rebel camps, took Zhengyang Pass, and was granted the title Kengse Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Following up, he combined land and river forces, destroyed more than forty rebel camps, retook Zhengyang Pass, and was granted the title Kengse Batulu.

sentences.zh: 閏五月，捻匪复踞正陽關，欽差大臣勝保率兵至八里垛，光箸請夾擊於沫河口，建浮橋先渡馬隊。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month Nian bandits again occupied Zhengyang Pass; Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao led troops to Baliduo; Guangzhu requested a pincer attack at Mohe Mouth and built a pontoon bridge to ferry the cavalry across first.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month the Nian reoccupied Zhengyang Pass. Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao brought troops to Baliduo. Guangzhu proposed a pincer at Mohe Mouth and threw a pontoon bridge to get the cavalry across first.

sentences.zh: 賊忽由後路鈔來，光箸立船頭督戰，左腿中槍，猶指揮進擊，纜斷溜急，舟覆，沒於河。

translations.literal: Rebels suddenly came around from the rear; Guangzhu stood on the boat's bow to direct battle, was shot in the left leg, still commanded the advance, the mooring rope broke and the current was swift, the boat capsized, and he drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels suddenly struck from the rear. Guangzhu stood on the bow directing the fight, was shot in the left leg, and still ordered the advance. The mooring rope snapped in the swift current, the boat capsized, and he drowned.

sentences.zh: 詔贈布政使銜，依贈官賜卹，予騎都尉世職，諡剛愍，於壽州建專祠。

translations.literal: An edict granted the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner, condolence according to the posthumous rank, the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, the posthumous title Gangmin, and a dedicated shrine at Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gave him the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner, mourning grants according to that rank, the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, the posthumous title Gangmin, and a memorial shrine at Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 光箸吏治戰績為安徽第一。

translations.literal: Guangzhu's administrative governance and battle achievements ranked first in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhu's civil administration and military record ranked first in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「大兵宜攻不宜守。

translations.literal: He once said: "Great armies should attack and not merely defend.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Main armies should attack, not merely hold defensive positions.

sentences.zh: 郡縣吏宜守四境，不宜守孤城。」

translations.literal: Prefectural and county officials should defend the four borders and should not merely defend an isolated city."
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates should hold the whole territory, not merely cling to an isolated walled city."

sentences.zh: 皖北倚為保障。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui relied on him as its bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Anhui had relied on him as its shield.

sentences.zh: 及其歿後，捻氛乃益熾，人尤思之雲。

translations.literal: After his death the Nian atmosphere grew still more fierce, and people especially missed him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Nian power grew fiercer still, and people missed him all the more.

sentences.zh: =李孟群=李孟群，字鶴人，河南光州人。

translations.literal: = Li Mengqun = Li Mengqun, styled Heren, was a native of Guangzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengqun, styled Heren, was from Guangzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父卿穀，道光二年舉人，四川長寧知縣，累擢湖北督糧道，署按察使。

translations.literal: His father Qinggu was a provincial graduate in the second year of Daoguang, magistrate of Changning in Sichuan, and was repeatedly promoted to grain transport commissioner of Hubei and acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinggu became a provincial graduate in the second year of Daoguang, served as magistrate of Changning in Sichuan, and rose to Hubei's grain transport commissioner and acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，粵匪陷武昌，巡撫青麟走湖南，卿穀守城殉難，贈布政使，予騎都尉世職，諡愍肅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng the Guangdong rebels took Wuchang; Governor Qinglin fled to Hunan; Qinggu defended the city and died in martyrdom; he was posthumously made provincial administration commissioner, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Minsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng the rebels took Wuchang. Governor Qinglin fled to Hunan while Qinggu held the city and died in its defense. He was posthumously made provincial administration commissioner, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Minsu.

sentences.zh: 孟群，道光二十七年進士，廣西即用知縣。

translations.literal: Mengqun was a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang and a magistrate on immediate assignment in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqun became a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang and was posted as a magistrate on immediate assignment in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 歷署靈川、桂平，以剿匪功擢南寧同知。

translations.literal: He successively acted at Lingchuan and Guiping; for merit in suppressing bandits he was promoted to subprefect of Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Lingchuan and Guiping in turn and was promoted to subprefect of Nanning for suppressing bandits.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，匪首洪秀全犯盤龍河，孟群手執藤牌督戰殺賊，鏖戰連日，賊不得渡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the bandit chief Hong Xiuquan attacked Panlong River; Mengqun personally held a rattan shield to direct battle and kill rebels; they fought fiercely for days, and the rebels could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng the rebel chief Hong Xiuquan attacked Panlong River. Mengqun took up a rattan shield himself to lead the fight, battled for days on end, and kept the rebels from crossing.

sentences.zh: 擢知府，調赴永安軍營。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect and transferred to the Yong'an military camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect and sent to the Yong'an army camp.

sentences.zh: 二年，授泗城知府。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed prefect of Sicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed prefect of Sicheng.

sentences.zh: 賊犯桂林，孟群赴援，連戰北門外及古牛山、五里墟、夾山口、睦鄰村，迭挫賊鋒。

translations.literal: When rebels attacked Guilin, Mengqun went to reinforce; he fought repeatedly outside the north gate and at Guniu Mountain, Wulixu, Jiashankou, and Mulincun, repeatedly blunting the rebel spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Guilin, Mengqun marched to reinforce. He fought outside the north gate and at Guniu Mountain, Wulixu, Jiashankou, and Mulincun, beating back the rebels again and again.

sentences.zh: 圍解，加道銜。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted he was given a brevet intendant's rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was lifted he received a brevet intendant's rank.

sentences.zh: 進平潯州艇匪，擢道員，署潯州知府。

translations.literal: Advancing, he pacified the boat bandits of Xunzhou, was promoted to intendant, and acted as prefect of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the boat bandits of Xunzhou, was promoted to intendant, and acted as prefect of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，調江西九江府，仍留廣西勦賊。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Jiujiang Prefecture in Jiangxi but remained in Guangxi to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Jiujiang in Jiangxi but stayed on in Guangxi to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 四年，曾國籓在籍治水師，聞孟群名，奏調率千人往偕楊載福、彭玉麟東下，攻拔城陵磯，克岳州，調廣西平樂府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zeng Guofan at home was organizing a naval force; hearing Mengqun's name, he memorialized to transfer him to lead a thousand men east with Yang Zaifu and Peng Yulin, captured Chenglingji, took Yuezhou, and was transferred to Pingle Prefecture in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zeng Guofan, at home organizing a naval force, heard of Mengqun and had him called up with a thousand men to join Yang Zaifu and Peng Yulin on the eastern campaign. They took Chenglingji and Yuezhou, and Mengqun was transferred to Pingle Prefecture in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 賊陷武昌，孟群聞父殉難，誓滅賊復仇，仍請終制，詔留軍。

translations.literal: When rebels took Wuchang, Mengqun heard his father had died in martyrdom, swore to destroy the rebels and take revenge, still requested to complete mourning, and an edict ordered him to remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell, Mengqun learned his father had died defending the city, swore to destroy the rebels in revenge, asked to complete mourning, and was ordered by edict to stay with the army.

sentences.zh: 國籓屯金口，塔奇布進扼洪山，定三路攻武昌之策。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan encamped at Jinkou; Taqiibu advanced to hold Hongshan, and a plan to attack Wuchang on three routes was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan encamped at Jinkou while Taqiibu advanced to hold Hongshan, and they fixed a three-pronged plan to retake Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 孟群偕載福、玉麟中流直下，艦分二隊，前隊沖鹽關出賊背，後隊自上擊下，毀賊船二百餘艘。

translations.literal: Mengqun with Zaifu and Yulin drove straight down the midstream; the fleet divided into two squadrons—the vanguard charged through Yanguan to emerge behind the rebels, the rear squadron struck from above downward, and destroyed more than two hundred rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqun with Zaifu and Yulin drove down the midstream. The fleet split in two: the vanguard charged through Yanguan to hit the rebels from behind, the rear squadron struck from above, and they destroyed more than two hundred rebel boats.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍剷沿江木柵，破漢關及金沙洲、白沙洲，抵鮎魚套，西渡攻漢陽朝宗門。

translations.literal: Together with the armies they cleared the wooden barriers along the river, broke Hankou Pass and Jinshazhou and Baishazhou, reached Nianyutao, crossed west to attack Hanyang's Chaozong Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the land forces they cleared the river barriers, broke through Hankou Pass, Jinshazhou, and Baishazhou, reached Nianyutao, and crossed west to attack Hanyang's Chaozong Gate.

sentences.zh: 賊揚帆下竄，屍蔽江。

translations.literal: The rebels set sail and fled downstream; corpses covered the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled downstream under sail, and corpses covered the river.

sentences.zh: 毀晴川閣下木柵、大別山下木壘，武昌、漢陽同日收復。

translations.literal: They destroyed the wooden barrier below Qingchuan Pavilion and the wooden fort below Dabie Mountain; Wuchang and Hanyang were recovered the same day.
translations.idiomatic: They destroyed the wooden defenses below Qingchuan Pavilion and Dabie Mountain, and Wuchang and Hanyang were retaken the same day.

sentences.zh: 孟群奔赴父死所慟哭收殮，一軍感動。

translations.literal: Mengqun hurried to where his father had died, wept bitterly, and gathered the remains; the whole army was moved.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqun rushed to where his father had fallen, wept as he gathered the remains, and moved the whole army.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加按察使銜，賜號珠爾杭阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was given the brevet rank of provincial judicial commissioner and granted the title Zhu'erhang'a Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he received the brevet rank of provincial judicial commissioner and the title Zhu'erhang'a Batulu.

sentences.zh: 於是國籓進規江西，孟群率水師抵九江，戰兩岸及湖口皆捷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zeng Guofan advanced to plan against Jiangxi; Mengqun led the naval force to Jiujiang and was victorious in battles on both banks and at Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan then advanced into Jiangxi. Mengqun led the fleet to Jiujiang and won victories on both banks and at Hukou.

sentences.zh: 五年春，師挫於湖口，賊溯江上犯，陷漢陽，武昌大震。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year the army was checked at Hukou; rebels moved upriver to attack, took Hanyang, and Wuchang was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year the army was beaten at Hukou. The rebels moved upriver, took Hanyang, and panic spread through Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 孟群回援，偕彭玉麟敗賊漢陽。

translations.literal: Mengqun returned to reinforce and with Peng Yulin defeated the rebels at Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqun returned to reinforce and, with Peng Yulin, defeated the rebels at Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 署湖北按察使，以在憂辭，詔不允。

translations.literal: He acted as provincial judicial commissioner of Hubei; citing mourning he declined, but an edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as Hubei's provincial judicial commissioner, pleaded mourning duties, and was refused by edict.

sentences.zh: 武昌尋為賊陷，從胡林翼屯金口，改統陸師。

translations.literal: Wuchang was soon taken by rebels; he followed Hu Linyi in encamping at Jinkou and was changed to command the land army.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang soon fell again. He joined Hu Linyi at Jinkou and was put in command of the land forces.

sentences.zh: 五月，合擊賊，四戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they joined to attack the rebels and were victorious in four battles.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they joined in an attack and won four battles in a row.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊糾黨撲金口，孟群拒戰失利，陸營潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month rebels gathered followers and rushed Jinkou; Mengqun resisted but was defeated and the land camp collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels rallied their forces against Jinkou. Mengqun fought them off but was beaten and the land camp broke.

sentences.zh: 詔以眾寡不敵原之，命攻漢陽。

translations.literal: An edict excused him on grounds that few could not match many and ordered him to attack Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict excused the defeat on grounds of overwhelming odds and ordered him to attack Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，從總督官文迭進攻，十一月，孟群據龜山俯擊，總兵王國才攻西南各門，城中賊亂，遂克漢陽，加布政使銜，以布政使遇缺題奏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Governor Guan Wen in repeated advances; in the eleventh month Mengqun held Guishan to strike downward, Regional Commander Wang Guocai attacked the southwest gates, rebels in the city fell into disorder, and Hanyang was taken; he was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner and was to be memorialized for substantive appointment when a vacancy occurred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he followed Governor Guan Wen in repeated assaults. In the eleventh month Mengqun held Guishan and struck downward while Regional Commander Wang Guocai attacked the southwest gates. The rebels in the city fell into disorder and Hanyang was taken. He received the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner and was marked for substantive appointment when a vacancy opened.

sentences.zh: 七年，安徽北路捻匪方熾，粵匪自桐城進陷六安、英山、霍山，廬州危急。
