translations.literal: In the seventh year Nian bandits on the northern route of Anhui were fiercely active; Guangdong rebels from Tongcheng advanced and took Lu'an, Yingshan, and Huoshan, and Luzhou was critical.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Nian bandits were raging along northern Anhui while rebels from Tongcheng took Lu'an, Yingshan, and Huoshan. Luzhou was in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福濟請援，孟群率陸師二千五百人赴之，途次授安徽布政使。

translations.literal: Governor Fuiji requested aid; Mengqun led twenty-five hundred land troops to go, and en route was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fuiji asked for reinforcements. Mengqun marched with twenty-five hundred land troops and was appointed Anhui's provincial administration commissioner on the way.

sentences.zh: 進兵克英山、霍山，攻獨山，駐軍麻埠。

translations.literal: Advancing his army he took Yingshan and Huoshan, attacked Dushan, and stationed troops at Mapu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, took Yingshan and Huoshan, attacked Dushan, and camped at Mapu.

sentences.zh: 霍山復為賊陷，尋復之。

translations.literal: Huoshan was again taken by rebels, but soon he recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Huoshan fell again to the rebels, but he soon retook it.

sentences.zh: 八年，粵匪由潛山、太湖竄擾河南固始。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Guangdong rebels from Qianshan and Taihu raided Gushi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year rebels from Qianshan and Taihu raided Gushi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 孟群自六安赴援，偕勝保力戰解圍，被獎敘。

translations.literal: Mengqun went from Lu'an to reinforce, fought hard with Sheng Bao to lift the siege, and was rewarded with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqun marched from Lu'an to reinforce, fought hard with Sheng Bao to lift the siege, and was commended for it.

sentences.zh: 剿商城匪黨，平之，回軍克六安。

translations.literal: He suppressed bandit factions at Shangcheng and pacified them, then returned his army and took Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the bandits at Shangcheng, pacified them, and on his return took Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 七月，福濟卒於軍，暫攝巡撫，未十日，廬州為粵匪所陷，褫職，留軍​​效力。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Fuiji died in the army; Mengqun temporarily acted as governor; within ten days Luzhou was taken by Guangdong rebels; he was stripped of office but remained with the army to serve.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Fuiji died in camp. Mengqun briefly acted as governor, but within ten days Luzhou fell to the rebels. He was stripped of rank but kept on with the army.

sentences.zh: 收集潰軍，駐廬州西官亭、長城一帶。

translations.literal: He gathered the collapsed troops and was stationed around Guanting and Changcheng west of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the broken troops and camped around Guanting and Changcheng west of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 皖北赤地千里，協餉不至，所部號四千，飢疲已甚。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui was barren for a thousand li; coordinated pay did not arrive; his command numbered four thousand on paper, and hunger and exhaustion were extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Anhui was a wasteland for a thousand li, pay never arrived, his force numbered four thousand on paper, and hunger and exhaustion were extreme.

sentences.zh: 湘軍李續賓方克桐城、舒城，飛書乞援，而續賓戰歿於三河，勢益孤危。

translations.literal: The Hunan Army's Li Xubin had just taken Tongcheng and Shucheng and sent a urgent letter begging aid, but Xubin died in battle at Sanhe, and the situation grew still more isolated and perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin of the Hunan Army had just taken Tongcheng and Shucheng and sent an urgent plea for help, but Xubin was killed at Sanhe and Mengqun's position grew still more desperate.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，六安复陷，賊六七萬逼長城，營壘被圍，死守十餘日。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year Lu'an fell again; sixty or seventy thousand rebels pressed Changcheng; the camps were besieged and held firm for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year Lu'an fell again. Sixty or seventy thousand rebels pressed Changcheng, besieged the camps, and held them under siege for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 壘破，手刃數賊，受傷被執，擁至廬州，賊首陳玉成優禮之，絕糧不食，賦詩四章書於絹，付人使出報大營，遂死之。

translations.literal: When the fortifications broke he personally killed several rebels, was wounded and captured, was taken to Luzhou; the rebel chief Chen Yucheng treated him with courtesy; he refused food and starved; he composed four poems on silk and sent someone out to report to the main camp, and thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: When the lines broke he killed several rebels with his own hand, was wounded and captured, and taken to Luzhou. Rebel chief Chen Yucheng treated him with respect, but he refused food and starved. He wrote four poems on silk, sent a messenger to report to headquarters, and died.

sentences.zh: 勝保等先已疏陳孟群殺賊陣亡，詔復原官，賜卹，諡武愍。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao and others had already memorialized that Mengqun had killed rebels and died in battle; an edict restored his original office, granted condolence, and gave the posthumous title Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao and others had already reported that Mengqun had died fighting the rebels. An edict restored his rank, granted mourning honors, and gave him the posthumous title Wumin.

sentences.zh: 十年，巡撫翁同書以尋獲遺骸入奏，命送回籍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Governor Weng Tonghe memorialized that the remains had been found and ordered them sent back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Governor Weng Tonghe reported that his remains had been found and ordered them sent home.

sentences.zh: 袁甲三復奏孟群死事實跡，詔於廬州建專祠，依巡撫例優恤，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiasan again memorialized the true circumstances of Mengqun's death; an edict ordered a dedicated shrine at Luzhou, preferential mourning according to the precedent for governors, and the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Captain together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiasan again described the circumstances of Mengqun's death. An edict ordered a memorial shrine at Luzhou, mourning honors on the governor's scale, and the combined hereditary ranks of Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以孟群父子殉節，忠烈萃於一門，與賜祭死事諸臣之列焉。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne, because father and son Mengqun had died in loyal martyrdom and fierce loyalty gathered in one family, he was placed among the officials granted sacrificial rites for death in service.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, father and son were honored together for dying in loyal service, and Mengqun was placed among the officials granted state sacrifice.

sentences.zh: =趙景賢=趙景賢，字竹生，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: = Zhao Jingxian = Zhao Jingxian, styled Zhusheng, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingxian, styled Zhusheng, was from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父炳言，嘉慶二十二年進士，授刑部主事，歷官湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Bingyan was a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing, appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, and rose to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bingyan became a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing, entered the Ministry of Justice as a clerk, and rose to governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 景賢，道光二十四年舉人，誤註烏程籍，被黜。

translations.literal: Jingxian was a provincial graduate in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang; mistakenly registered under Wucheng domicile, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian received his provincial degree in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang but was disqualified for registering under the wrong domicile.

sentences.zh: 捐复，授宣平教諭，改內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased restoration, was appointed instructor at Xuanping, and was changed to secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He bought reinstatement, was made instructor at Xuanping, and then secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 豪邁有大略。

translations.literal: He was bold and possessed great strategic vision.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，在籍倡團練，以勸捐鉅款，晉秩知府，分發甘肅，未往。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, while at home he initiated militia training; for urging large donations he was advanced to prefect, assigned to Gansu, but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he organized militia at home, raised large donations, was promoted to prefect, and was assigned to Gansu but never went.

sentences.zh: 十年，尚書許乃普薦之，命從​​團練大臣邵燦治事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Minister Xu Naipu recommended him and he was ordered to follow Militia Commissioner Shao Can in handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Minister Xu Naipu recommended him, and he was ordered to serve under Militia Commissioner Shao Can.

sentences.zh: 聞粵匪陷廣德，自蘇州馳歸，籌布守城。

translations.literal: Hearing Guangdong rebels had taken Guangde, he hurried back from Suzhou and planned the city's defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that rebels had taken Guangde, he rushed back from Suzhou to organize the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 總兵李定太、參將周天孚先後來援失利。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Li Dingtai and Brigadier Zhou Tianfu came in succession to reinforce but suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Li Dingtai and Brigadier Zhou Tianfu came to reinforce in turn but were beaten.

sentences.zh: 景賢收集潰兵，為戰守計。

translations.literal: Jingxian gathered the collapsed troops and made plans for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian gathered the broken troops and planned for defense.

sentences.zh: 偵知江南援軍至，出城夾擊，擒斬數千，立解城圍。

translations.literal: Learning that Jiangnan relief troops had arrived, he went out of the city to attack from both sides, captured and killed several thousand, and the siege was at once lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jiangnan relief troops had arrived, he sallied out in a pincer attack, killed several thousand, and lifted the siege at once.

sentences.zh: 從張玉良复杭州，克長興、德清、武康。

translations.literal: He followed Zhang Yuliang in recovering Hangzhou and took Changxing, Deqing, and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhang Yuliang in retaking Hangzhou and captured Changxing, Deqing, and Wukang.

sentences.zh: 既而賊擾嘉興，景賢分兵屯南潯，扼其衝。

translations.literal: Before long rebels harassed Jiaxing; Jingxian divided troops to encamp at Nanxun and block their thrust.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels then raided Jiaxing. Jingxian posted troops at Nanxun to block their advance.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊由太湖、夾浦犯湖州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month rebels from Taihu and Jiapu attacked Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month rebels from Taihu and Jiapu attacked Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 道員蕭翰慶來援，戰歿，招其潰兵入伍，出北門擊賊，血戰數晝夜，賊遁。

translations.literal: Intendant Xiao Hanqing came to reinforce and died in battle; Jingxian recruited his collapsed troops into his ranks, went out the north gate to strike rebels, fought bloody battles for several days and nights, and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Intendant Xiao Hanqing came to reinforce and was killed. Jingxian took in his broken troops, sallied from the north gate, fought bloody battles for days, and drove the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 五月，率砲船進攻平望鎮，與楚軍合擊，克之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he led gunboats to attack Pingwang Town, joined with the Chu army in a combined strike, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he led gunboats against Pingwang Town, joined the Hunan army in a combined assault, and took it.

sentences.zh: 會賊酋陳玉成由溧水竄浙境，景賢回救，合民團要擊走之，賜號額爾德木巴圖魯，以道員用。

translations.literal: Meanwhile rebel chief Chen Yucheng fled from Lishui into Zhejiang territory; Jingxian returned to rescue, combined with local militia to intercept and drive him off, was granted the title E'erdemu Batulu, and was employed as intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Chen Yucheng then broke into Zhejiang from Lishui. Jingxian rushed back, joined local militia in an intercepting action, and drove him off. He was granted the title E'erdemu Batulu and employed as intendant.

sentences.zh: 六月，進复廣德，交軍機處記名簡放。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he advanced to recover Guangde and was noted by name at the Grand Council for direct appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he retook Guangde and was marked for direct appointment by the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊犯杭州，景賢馳援。

translations.literal: In the tenth month rebels attacked Hangzhou and Jingxian hurried to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month rebels attacked Hangzhou and Jingxian rushed to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 湖州告警，速回師，賊已至南門外峴山。

translations.literal: Huzhou sounded the alarm; he quickly returned his army, but rebels had already reached Xianshan outside the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhou sounded the alarm and he turned back quickly, but rebels had already reached Xianshan outside the south gate.

sentences.zh: 副將劉仁福率廣勇來援，有通賊狀，誘擒仁福，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Brigadier Liu Renfu led Guang braves to reinforce; there was evidence he communicated with rebels; Jingxian lured and seized Renfu and beheaded him as warning.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier Liu Renfu came with Guang volunteers but was suspected of dealing with the rebels. Jingxian lured him in, seized him, and executed him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 賊奪氣，分擾四鄉，旋犯西門。

translations.literal: The rebels lost spirit, split to harass the four townships, and soon attacked the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lost heart, split to raid the countryside, and soon struck the west gate.

sentences.zh: 合水陸擊退，盡破附近諸山賊壘，圍复解，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: He combined land and water forces to drive them back, completely broke the rebel fortifications on the nearby mountains, the siege was again lifted, and he was given the brevet rank of provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He combined land and river forces to beat them back, destroyed the nearby mountain forts, lifted the siege again, and received the brevet rank of provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复長興。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he recovered Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he retook Changxing.

sentences.zh: 尋賊踞洞庭東、西兩山，長興不能守，郡北七十二漊時被擾。

translations.literal: Before long rebels occupied the eastern and western mountains of Dongting; Changxing could not be held, and the seventy-two creeks north of the prefecture were harassed from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels soon seized the eastern and western hills of Dongting. Changxing could not be held, and the seventy-two creeks north of the prefecture were raided repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 景賢於大錢口增駐水師，聯絡民團，分顧各路，屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Jingxian increased the naval garrison at Daqiankou, linked with local militia, divided attention among the various routes, and was victorious in repeated battles.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian reinforced the naval post at Daqiankou, coordinated with local militia, covered every approach, and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊踞菱湖鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month rebels occupied Linghu Town.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rebels seized Linghu Town.

sentences.zh: 率水師進攻，毀賊舟，又破之於澉山溪。

translations.literal: He led the naval force in attack, destroyed rebel boats, and defeated them again at Ganshan Creek.
translations.idiomatic: He led the fleet in attack, destroyed rebel boats, and defeated them again at Ganshan Creek.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊又逼郡城，鏖戰五晝夜，追奔出境。

translations.literal: In the ninth month rebels again pressed the prefectural city; he fought fiercely for five days and nights and pursued them fleeing beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month rebels pressed the prefectural city again. He fought for five days and nights and drove them beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 時杭州久被困，景賢率兵滾營前進，連破賊卡二十餘處。

translations.literal: At that time Hangzhou had long been besieged; Jingxian led troops forward in rolling camps and in succession broke more than twenty rebel checkpoints.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou had long been besieged. Jingxian advanced in rolling camps and broke more than twenty rebel checkpoints in succession.

sentences.zh: 賊复乘虛襲大錢口，景賢且戰且退，掩擊之，賊遁。

translations.literal: Rebels again took advantage of a gap to strike Daqiankou; Jingxian fought while retreating, then struck from ambush, and the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels again struck Daqiankou while he was away. Jingxian fought as he fell back, then hit them in ambush and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 聞杭州再陷，歎曰：「湖郡孤注，惟當效死弗去，以報國恩耳！」

translations.literal: Hearing Hangzhou had fallen again, he sighed and said: "Huzhou Prefecture stands alone; I can only die without leaving, to repay the state's grace!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Hangzhou had fallen again, he sighed and said, "Huzhou stands alone now. I can only die in place and repay the state's grace!"

sentences.zh: 是年冬，授福建督糧道。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed grain transport commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed Fujian's grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年春，詔念景賢殺賊守城，於團練中功稱最，特加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Tongzhi an edict recalled that Jingxian had killed rebels and defended the city, that among militia his merit was called the greatest, and specially added the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Tongzhi an edict noted that among militia leaders his record of killing rebels and holding the city was unmatched, and specially gave him the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自賊氛逼城，僅大錢口可通太湖糧道。

translations.literal: Since rebel atmosphere pressed the city, only Daqiankou could keep open the grain route on Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: Once rebels pressed the city, only Daqiankou still connected it to the Taihu grain route.

sentences.zh: 會大雪湖凍，賊由洞庭東山履冰來犯，大錢遂為所踞。

translations.literal: Meanwhile heavy snow froze the lake; rebels from Dongting's eastern hill came attacking over the ice, and Daqiankou was thereupon occupied.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow then froze the lake. Rebels from Dongting's eastern hill crossed the ice to attack, and Daqiankou fell.

sentences.zh: 賊以屢戰傷亡多，恨景賢次骨，掘其父墓，戒不與戰，但斷絕糧道以困之。

translations.literal: Because repeated battles had cost many casualties, the rebels hated Jingxian to the marrow, dug up his father's tomb, forbade battle with him, and only cut off the grain route to wear him down.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost heavily in repeated battles, the rebels hated Jingxian to the bone, dug up his father's tomb, avoided fighting him directly, and only cut his grain route to starve him out.

sentences.zh: 景賢迭出戰不利，密寄帛書至上海與其叔炳麟訣，誓以死守。

translations.literal: Jingxian went out to battle repeatedly without success, secretly sent a silk letter to Shanghai to bid farewell to his uncle Binglin, and swore to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian sallied out repeatedly without success, secretly sent a farewell letter on silk to his uncle Binglin in Shanghai, and swore to hold the city to the death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惜其才，命曾國籓、左宗棠設法傳諭輕裝出赴任，景賢益感奮，選壯士三千人，分出斫賊營，奪其糧而還。

translations.literal: The court valued his talent and ordered Zeng Guofan and Zuo Zongtang to find means to transmit orders that he go lightly equipped to take his post; Jingxian was still more stirred to zeal, selected three thousand stalwart men, sent detachments to cut rebel camps, seized their grain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court valued his talent and had Zeng Guofan and Zuo Zongtang urge him to leave lightly equipped for his new post. Stirred all the more, he picked three thousand stalwarts, sent raiding parties to cut rebel camps, seized their grain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 被圍既久，兵日給米二合五勺，官民皆食粥糜，道殣相望。

translations.literal: Besieged for a long time, soldiers were given two and a half he of rice daily; officials and people all ate thin gruel; corpses lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The siege wore on. Soldiers received two and a half he of rice a day; officials and civilians lived on thin gruel; corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 五月，城陷。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the city fell.

sentences.zh: 景賢冠帶見賊，曰：「速殺我，勿傷百姓。」

translations.literal: Jingxian in cap and belt went to see the rebels and said: "Kill me quickly; do not harm the people."
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian went out in full dress to face the rebels and said, "Kill me quickly and do not harm the people."

sentences.zh: 賊首譚紹洸曰：「亦不殺汝。」

translations.literal: The rebel chief Tan Shaoguang said: "Nor will I kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Tan Shaoguang said, "Nor will I kill you."

sentences.zh: 拔刀自刎，為所奪，執至蘇州，誘脅百端，皆不屈。

translations.literal: He drew his sword to cut his own throat but it was seized from him; he was taken to Suzhou, tempted and coerced in every way, and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword to kill himself, but they seized it, took him to Suzhou, and tried every form of persuasion and coercion without breaking him.

sentences.zh: 羈之逾半載，李秀成必欲降之，致書相勸。

translations.literal: He was detained for more than half a year; Li Xiucheng was determined to win his surrender and sent a letter to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: They held him for more than half a year. Li Xiucheng was determined to win him over and sent a letter of persuasion.

sentences.zh: 景賢復書略曰：「某受國恩，萬勿他說。

translations.literal: Jingxian replied in brief: "I have received the state's grace; speak no other word.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian replied in brief, "I owe the state a debt of grace. Say nothing else.

sentences.zh: 張睢陽慷慨成仁，文信國從容取義，私心竊嚮往之。

translations.literal: Zhang Suiyang achieved benevolence through generous martyrdom, Wen Xinguo took righteousness with calm composure—in my private heart I have long looked up to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suiyang died generously for principle, and Wen Tianxiang met death with calm resolve. In my heart I have long looked to them as models.

sentences.zh: 若隳節一時，貽笑萬世，雖甚不才，斷不為此也。

translations.literal: If I destroyed my integrity for a moment I would be laughed at for ten thousand generations; however very unworthy I am, I absolutely will not do this.
translations.idiomatic: To break my integrity for a moment would be to earn the laughter of ten thousand generations. However unworthy I am, I will never do that.

sentences.zh: 來書引及洪承疇、錢謙益、馮銓輩，當日已為士林所不齒，清議所不容。

translations.literal: Your letter cites Hong Chengchou, Qian Qianyi, Feng Quan, and the like; in their own day they were already despised by the scholarly class and intolerable to pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter cites Hong Chengchou, Qian Qianyi, Feng Quan, and men like them. Even in their own day the scholarly world despised them and upright opinion would not tolerate them.

sentences.zh: 純皇帝御定貳臣傳，名在首列。

translations.literal: The Pure Emperor in his imperially determined Biographies of Twice-Serving Ministers placed their names in the foremost rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor's imperial Biographies of Twice-Serving Ministers places their names at the very top.

sentences.zh: 此等人何足比數哉？

translations.literal: How are men of this sort fit to be counted in comparison?
translations.idiomatic: How can men like that be held up for comparison?

sentences.zh: 國家定制，失城者斬。

translations.literal: The state's fixed regulation is that one who loses a city is beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: By the law of the state, an official who loses a city is beheaded.

sentences.zh: 死於法，何若死於忠。

translations.literal: To die by the law—how does that compare with dying for loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Death under the law cannot compare with death for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 泰山鴻毛，審之久矣。

translations.literal: Mount Tai and a goose feather—I have weighed this long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Tai and a goose feather—I settled that question long ago.

sentences.zh: 左右果然見愛，則歸我者為知己，不如殺我者尤為知己也。」

translations.literal: If you truly regard me with affection, then one who returns me is a confidant—but one who kills me is an even better confidant."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly care for me, then the friend who sends me home is a confidant—but the friend who kills me is an even truer one."

sentences.zh: 秀成赴江北，戒紹洸勿殺。

translations.literal: Xiucheng went to Jiangbei and warned Shaoguang not to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng went to Jiangbei and ordered Shaoguang not to kill him.

sentences.zh: 景賢計欲伺隙手刃秀成，秀成去，日惟危坐飲酒。

translations.literal: Jingxian planned to wait for an opening to kill Xiucheng with his own hand; when Xiucheng left, he each day only sat upright and drank wine.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian planned to seize a chance to kill Xiucheng with his own hand. After Xiucheng left, he sat upright each day and drank.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，紹洸聞太倉敗賊言景賢通官軍，將襲蘇州，召詰之，景賢謾罵，為槍擊而殞。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year Shaoguang heard from defeated rebels at Taicang that Jingxian was in contact with the government army and would attack Suzhou; he summoned and questioned him; Jingxian reviled him wildly and was shot and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year Shaoguang heard from defeated rebels at Taicang that Jingxian was in contact with the imperial army and planned to strike Suzhou. He summoned and questioned him; Jingxian cursed him furiously and was shot dead.

sentences.zh: 自湖州陷，屢有旨問景賢下落。

translations.literal: Since Huzhou fell, edicts repeatedly inquired after Jingxian's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: After Huzhou fell, the court repeatedly sent edicts asking for news of Jingxian.

sentences.zh: 至是死事上聞，詔稱其「勁節孤忠，可嘉可憫」，加恩依巡撫例優恤，於湖州建專祠，宣付史館為立特傳，予騎都尉世職，諡忠節。

translations.literal: When his death in service was reported to the throne, an edict praised his "firm integrity and solitary loyalty, worthy of praise and compassion," added grace with preferential mourning according to the precedent for governors, ordered a dedicated shrine at Huzhou, directed the Historiographical Office to compose a special biography, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave the posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached court, an edict praised his "unyielding integrity and steadfast loyalty, worthy of honor and pity," granted mourning honors on the governor's scale, ordered a memorial shrine at Huzhou, directed the Historiographical Office to write a special biography, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 長子深彥，年十二，在湖南，聞湖州陷，即自酖死。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shenyan, twelve years old, in Hunan, hearing Huzhou had fallen, at once took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shenyan, twelve years old and in Hunan, heard that Huzhou had fallen and took poison at once.

sentences.zh: 先被旌，附祀景賢祠。

translations.literal: He had earlier been commended and was given attendant sacrifice at Jingxian's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been honored and was given a place in sacrifice at Jingxian's shrine.

sentences.zh: 次子濱彥，賜官主事；

translations.literal: The second son Binyan was granted the office of principal clerk;
translations.idiomatic: The second son Binyan was granted the rank of principal clerk;

sentences.zh: 溱彥、淶彥皆以通判用。

translations.literal: Qinyan and Laiyan were both employed as subprefects.
translations.idiomatic: Qinyan and Laiyan were both appointed subprefects.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：何桂珍儒臣出為監司，以忠義激勵飢軍，竟撫悍寇；

translations.literal: = Commentary = The commentary says: He Guizhen, a Confucian minister who went out as a surveillance commissioner, roused starving troops with loyalty and righteousness and in the end pacified fierce bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He Guizhen was a scholar-official sent out as a circuit intendant. He roused starving troops with appeals to loyalty and righteousness and even pacified fierce bandits;

sentences.zh: 誤於庸帥，倉猝殞身。

translations.literal: he was undone by a mediocre commander and perished in haste.
translations.idiomatic: but a mediocre commander undid him, and he died before his time.

sentences.zh: 徐豐玉才裕匡濟，兵單致敗。

translations.literal: Xu Fengyu had talent ample enough to aid the age, but few troops brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fengyu had talent enough to steady the times, but too few troops brought defeat.

sentences.zh: 溫紹原守六合，金光箸守壽州，並以彈丸一邑，出奇制勝，砥柱狂瀾，其有關於江淮全局者大矣。

translations.literal: Wen Shaoyuan defended Liuhe and Jin Guangzhu defended Shouzhou; both with a pellet-sized single county won by unexpected stratagems, stood as pillars against raging floods—their relevance to the overall situation on the Huai and Yangzi was great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shaoyuan held Liuhe and Jin Guangzhu held Shouzhou. Each defended a tiny county with bold stratagems and stood like pillars against the flood. Their importance to the whole Huai-Yangzi front was immense.

sentences.zh: 李孟群戰功卓著，至皖北兵食俱絀，卒不復振，父子繼死國事，為世所哀。

translations.literal: Li Mengqun's battle achievements were outstanding, but when in northern Anhui troops and provisions were both exhausted he ultimately could not recover; father and son died in succession for the state, and the age mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengqun's military record was outstanding, but in northern Anhui troops and supplies gave out and he could not recover. Father and son died in turn for the state, and the world mourned them.

sentences.zh: 趙景賢以鄉紳任戰守，殺敵致果，繼以忠貞。

translations.literal: Zhao Jingxian as a local gentry member undertook battle and defense, killed enemies to achieve resolution, and followed with loyal steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingxian, a local gentleman, took charge of defense, killed the enemy with resolve, and ended in steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 當時團練遍行省，自湖湘之外，收效者斯為僅見。

translations.literal: At that time militia training spread through the provinces; apart from Hunan and Hubei, those who achieved results were rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: Militia were raised throughout the provinces at the time, but outside Hunan and Hubei few achieved results like these.

sentences.zh: 諸人不幸以節烈終，未竟其勳略，惜哉！

translations.literal: These men unfortunately ended in fierce integrity, their merit and strategy unfinished—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: These men sadly died in loyal martyrdom before their achievements were complete. What a pity!
